text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mostly steady with price movements being confined to a narrow range as little incentive could be drawn from a lacklustre New York market. Some of the turnover came from against actuals trades but routine business was the order of the day with very little interest reported to trade arbitrage against New York raws. August ended unchanged at $307.00 per tonne, after ranging between $306 and $307.30. October was up 40 cents at $303.20 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York settled barely higher as trade scale down buying and light local short-covering blunted earlier losses and lifted the market over unchanged near the close, dealers said. May ended 0.01 cent/lb higher at 10.96 cents/lb, having ranged from 10.98 to 10.86. Most active July gained 0.03 cent/lb on the day to close at 10.88 cents/lb, while the outer months finished 0.02 lower to up 0.01 cent. Persistent speculative selling in the May/July spread kept the market under pressure during the first half of the day, when the spread traded from 0.11 to 0.07 before closing at 0.08. The locals expecting the market to break down under Wednesday's low of 10.87 basis May, covered short positions when they failed to locate sell stops at the day's low of 10.86 cents, dealers said. The trade remained an excellent buyer on a scale-down basis, it was added.

THAILAND - More Thai sugar mills closed for the 1996/97 crushing season as cane supplies increasingly dry up. The sugar crushing season started in November and is expected to last until May or June. As of April 10 a total of 12 out of 46 mills had stopped operations for the season, but more mills might have closed down during the Songkran holiday which ended on April 15. Sugar output as of April 10 reached 5.940 mn tonnes, raw value, down from 5.968 mn tonnes in the same period last year. The sugar yield is now unlikely to match that of last season's as the latest data showed the total to be not more than 102.9 kg per tonne of cane crushed, below 105.6 kg in the same period last year.

SOUTH AFRICA - Plentiful rainfall could boost South Africa's 1997/98 (May/April) sugar crop to about 2.5 mn tonnes, tel quel, allowing exports of over 1 mn tonnes, according to the USDA attache reporting from Pretoria. Sugar production rose to 2.4 mn tonnes during the 1996/97 milling season, up from 1.77 mn tonnes in 1995/96. Total cane supply in 1997/98 is estimated to be around 22 mn tonnes.

BELGIUM - In March, the meteorological office recorded above normal temperatures, a significant deficit of precipitation and an average number of hours of sunshine. Climatic conditions in March were very favourable for beet drillings with overall conditions being generally dry. Sowings started around March 13 and were completed in mid April. Total sowings in 1997 amount to around 102,000 ha, down from 104,000 ha in 1996.

China bought 15,000 tonnes of Thai raw sugar for prompt shipment, trade sources said. Misubishi supplied 10,000 tonnes while Cargill supplied the rest. The consignments will be used for tolling, trade sources said. China recently issued up to 500,000 tonnes of tolling licenses.

Bangladesh is to tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of white sugar in two equal shipments, traders said. The tender is to be held on April 19, with half the required amount to be shipped for June 30 and half for July 15, it was added. Earlier this month, Bangladesh bought 25,000 tonnes of white sugar at $346.90 per tonne c&f for shipment by June 9, again split into two equal cargoes.

Iran was reported to have bought 2 to 3 cargoes of white sugar in the past 3 days. Details were sketchy, but two 14,000 tonne cargoes for May 15/June 15 shipment were thought to have traded at $307.25 and $313.00 fob, and a further 14,000 tonnes for June 15/July 15 shipment at $351 c&f.
South Korea was in the market today for 14,000 tonnes of raws for May/June shipment, but results were unknown.

South Africa was apparently in the market to sell 54,000 tonnes for May shipment and 54,000 tonnes for June shipment and although it was rumored that part of this package was sold, details were lacking.
